decision.rationale: The documented validators and repository checks pass, but independently executed local probes and direct code-to-Exam comparison reproduce material false passes. Policy and authoritative replay/CAS state are not independently established; lifecycle completion bypasses the required human and protected-action graph and is restricted to one copy; cost acceptance lacks the required provider-backed usage, invoice, and reconciliation evidence; privacy trusts k-equivalence claims and has deterministic normalization gaps; and two declared migration recovery cases execute identical bytes. Zero blockers and majors is therefore not established.

findings.title: Policy and authoritative replay/CAS state can be supplied by the candidate or an ordinary record caller

reproductions.observed: ALLOW with credentialAccess=1, installationToken=1, providerRequest=1, and gitWrite=1 while the accepted policyDigest is b repeated 64 times, not an independently retrieved authorization-policy digest.
reproductions.expected: The selected policy path, revision, and digest must be independently anchored and byte-equal across the manifest, request, authority, credentials, delegation, assignment, and protected-action decision.

reproductions.case: Set makePrivacyGraph().policyDigest to f repeated 64 times without changing any signed inner record and call privacyGraphDecision.
reproductions.expected: A substituted retention/privacy policy digest must reject before corpus acceptance.

reproductions.case: Replace an otherwise positive authorization bundle's replayLedgerBytes with sealRecord({idempotencyKey:'other'}) and casHeadBytes with sealRecord({head:request.casHead}), then call authorizationDecision.
reproductions.observed: ALLOW with all four operational effects; the consumed replay and head record IDs are null.
reproductions.expected: Replay ledger and CAS head must be closed, current records from independently selected authoritative signing domains, not ordinary caller-signable records.

reproductions.case: Use public sealRecord to create a committed same-key replay ledger for a protected request, or an unused replay record for makeHumanAuthorityBundle(), and call the corresponding decision.
reproductions.observed: The protected action returns REPLAY_NOOP and the human authority returns ALLOW using the ordinary caller-created ledger.
reproductions.expected: Caller-created state must never establish committed replay, unused authority state, or current CAS state.

findings.analysis: The full manifest currently hash-checks policy files as package artifacts, but that is not the same as oracle-time independent policy selection and binding. The authorization oracle never compares authority.policyDigest to an authoritative policy artifact. Privacy schema-validates policyDigest but never compares it. Human authority compares candidate-local literals rather than supplied independently retrieved policy bytes and a verified revision. Replay ledgers and CAS heads are parsed with the public ordinary-record key; authorization does not enforce a closed replay/head schema or currentness before effects. These gaps directly defeat the canonical authoritative-state and complete-selector contracts.
findings.requiredFix: Add immutable authorization/retention policy inputs selected outside caller-controlled evidence, recompute their bytes and revision-bound digests, and bind them through every applicable record. Define closed replay-ledger and CAS-head schemas and independent current trust domains; verify record type, source, status, timestamps, request/idempotency binding, head lineage, and snapshot freshness. Remove ordinary record signing as a source of authoritative replay/CAS state. Add policy substitution, missing policy bytes, ordinary-signer replay/head, stale head, missing fields, and null-ID cases to the independently derived execution inventory.

findings.title: Lifecycle completion succeeds without human authority, protected authorization/replay/CAS, or a multi-copy disposition graph

reproduction.case: Parse makeLifecycleGraph('RC-FAILED-RUN','complete'), inspect its graph/inventory/request, and call lifecycleGraphDecision.
reproduction.observed: The graph contains no human-authority bundle, protected-action authorization bundle, authoritative replay ledger, CAS head, or atomic reservation. Its signed inventory contains exactly one copy; the oracle explicitly requires inventory.copies.length===1 and accepts one provider receipt. It returns deleted-tombstoned with effects.lifecycle=1.
reproduction.expected: Completion requires a current eligible-human disposition authority where required, one protected provider request and authoritative replay/CAS result per canonical copy/key tuple, independently verified ordered provider receipts, an ordered aggregate receipt, and a tombstone over a passing two-copy and raw-multikey graph.

findings.analysis: Receipt-before-aggregate-before-tombstone time checks exist, but the graph omits the governing authorization path and enforces the opposite of the canonical multi-copy requirement. Request and receipt records also omit the canonical full tuple bindings for target/policy/inventory, authority, copy kind, object/version/key, immutable request digest, and provider-resource/CAS snapshots. The package has no canonical PROVIDER-KEY-REGISTRY.candidate.json onboarding map required by the protected Exam; a generic provider trust entry is not the specified per-provider binding proof.
findings.requiredFix: Replace the single receipt fields with canonical ordered per-copy/per-key arrays. Require exact complete inventory equality, one current human disposition or permitted raw grant per tuple, one protected request per tuple, independent provider-resource and provider-control-plane snapshots, authoritative replay/CAS decisions, provider-registry-selected receipt proofs, ordered aggregate rows, and a matching tombstone. Execute passing two-copy and raw-multikey cases plus every missing, duplicate, reused, extra, tuple/key/provider/policy/target mismatch, restored race, crash cut, replay, and CAS-loss case with typed zero effects.

findings.title: Cost invoice and reconciliation acceptance lacks provider-backed evidence and closed cross-record lineage

reproduction.case: Call costDecision(makeCostGraph('invoice-at-close')) and costDecision(makeCostGraph('reconcile-at-24h')); inspect each recordsBytes row.
reproduction.observed: Both return ALLOW. The invoice row has IDs and billed/acknowledged timestamps but no signed provider proof, usage start/end timestamps, provider invoice bytes/digest, implementation or target revision, or usage-record lineage. The reconciliation row has no invoice bytes/digest, usage bytes/digest, variance record, predecessor/successor lineage, or provider proof. The round-three schemas directory and schemaCases inventory contain no COST-EVIDENCE or SPEND-AUTHORIZATION schema.
reproduction.expected: Each forecast, reservation, usage/accrual, provider invoice, variance, reconciliation, alert, shutdown, revocation, and restart artifact must pass its closed discriminator schema and signed semantic lineage; provider invoice/usage proof and actual bytes must bind the closed period, exact units, authorization, price, scope, revisions, provider/SKU, and timestamps.

findings.analysis: The monetary signature proves only that the local fixture money key signed a sparse row. String IDs and timestamps are treated as provider facts. Invoice and reconciliation decisions are derived from the first row's claimed IDs/times rather than independently verified provider usage and invoice bytes or a complete bidirectional ledger-to-provider graph. Green arithmetic vectors therefore do not establish truthful post-close reconciliation.
findings.requiredFix: Restore closed SPEND-AUTHORIZATION and COST-EVIDENCE schema families and validate every branch. Consume independently provider-signed usage and invoice bytes/proofs, exact usage intervals and units, invoice issue/acknowledgement times, variance and reconciliation successors, target/implementation revisions, and complete one-to-one lineage. Add missing/substituted provider proof, usage time, invoice bytes, usage/invoice mismatch, orphan provider line, orphan ledger line, predecessor gap/fork, stale reference, and late/unavailable-provider cases.

findings.title: Privacy recomputes linkage but trusts k-equivalence and permits deterministic identifier evasions

reproductions.case: Call privacyGraphDecision(makePrivacyGraph()) and inspect the prompt equivalenceClassSize values and source pool.
reproductions.observed: ACCEPT. Every prompt claims equivalenceClassSize=5, and the oracle only checks that the supplied integer is at least five; it never derives an equivalence class from the frozen source pool. The fixture source pool contains 100 rows but only one unique source text.
reproductions.expected: Named-entity, four-token, k-equivalence, top-1 linkage, and Wilson outcomes must all be independently recomputed from the frozen authorized source pool and prompt bytes.

reproductions.observed: Both return an empty array. normalizePrivacyText leaves U+2066 in the second string.
reproductions.expected: Digit-only phone numbers and identifier labels split by Unicode format controls must be detected or deterministically rejected under the revision-bound normalization policy.

findings.analysis: The top-1 linkage trials and Wilson result are now recomputed, which is a real improvement over R2. Closure is still incomplete because equivalenceClassSize remains caller authority and the detector normalizer removes only selected format controls. The phone expression requires separators, so a common ten-digit representation evades the declared phone class. The existing one-plain/one-evasion/one-boundary-per-class inventory is insufficient to expose these category boundaries.
findings.requiredFix: Define and execute the exact k-equivalence procedure over the frozen source pool and derive each prompt's class size; remove equivalenceClassSize as an accepted claim. Normalize or reject the complete governed Unicode format-control class with explicit safe exceptions, normalize phone digits before classification, and add digit-only, country-code, extension, Unicode-isolate/embedding/mark, joined-label, and precision-boundary fixtures. Keep the existing independently recomputed top-1/Wilson checks.

findings.title: Declared migration recovery and restore cases execute identical ordinary success evidence

reproduction.case: Compare makeMigrationFailureCase('recovery') with makeMigrationFailureCase('restore'), hash both, and run migrationDecision on each.
reproduction.observed: The two serialized graphs are byte-identical with SHA-256 2a8c3cf336b2d97bdf13c22fa33e2158985993b2d3133cc377da4a8890e80328. Both return the same journaled migration effect and tuple. The validator marks two distinct declared IDs without comparing per-ID input or result digests.
reproduction.expected: Recovery and restoration must be distinct signed execution graphs with their own reachable state, interruption, backup/PITR/restoration evidence, expected state/result/effects, and unique input/result digests.

findings.analysis: Exact declared-ID counting does not prove distinct semantic coverage when multiple IDs consume identical bytes and identical outcomes. The R2 resolution's statement that recovery and restore execute is therefore overstated.
findings.requiredFix: Materialize separate recovery and restoration fixtures and expected outcomes, bind them to unique execution/provider/journal/backup/restoration evidence, and compare each declared ID's input digest, result digest, state, first error, and typed effects against an independently derived expectation. Reject duplicate semantic evidence across distinct required cases.

targetedLocalObservations.ordinaryReplayAndHead: ALLOW or REPLAY_NOOP from public ordinary-record signatures
targetedLocalObservations.migrationRecoveryRestore: byte-identical inputs and identical journaled effects

priorR2ResolutionDisposition.details: The R2 resolution accurately records green package counts, but its technicalStatus=remediated claims for authoritative policy/state, lifecycle, monetary, privacy, and migration coverage are contradicted by the reproducible local observations above.

otherMaterialReview.details: No further independent blocker or major was identified in the bounded ordinary code/document comparison beyond the five findings recorded here. Passing accessibility and provider-recovery aggregates were not treated as actual human Gate 3 evidence or authorization.

requiredNextState: Correct every blocker and major and add the direct counterexamples to an independently derived normative inventory.
Freeze the corrected package and rerun both local remediation modes and pnpm check.
Obtain a new independent fresh-context zero-blocker/zero-major Critic before any protected incorporation.
After authorized incorporation, obtain the required new exact-revision qualified-human ruling and all seven fresh domain reviews before any eligible human Gate 2 decision.
